rows.text: # 2kg Country Sourdough Loaf ## Ingredients Total flour weight is 2000 g and all baker's percentages below are calculated against that total flour weight. Final hydration is 80%. | Ingredient | Weight | Baker's % | |---|---|---| | Strong white bread flour | 1700 g | 85% | | Wholemeal flour | 300 g | 15% | | Water (28C) | 1600 g | 80% | | Fine sea salt | 40 g | 2% | | Rye levain (100% hydration) | 400 g | 20% | Total dough weight is 4040 g, which divides into two loaves of roughly 2020 g each. ## Method Autolyse first. Combine the strong white flour, the wholemeal flour and 1500 g of the water in a large tub, mixing until no dry flour remains, then cover and rest for 60 minutes. Hold back the remaining 100 g of water for the salt stage. Add the rye levain and squeeze it through the dough until fully dispersed. Rest for 30 minutes. Now add the fine sea salt together with the reserved 100 g of water. The salt goes in after the autolyse and after the levain, never at the start, because salt tightens the gluten network and slows the enzymatic activity the autolyse is meant to encourage. Squeeze and fold until the dough feels smooth and no grittiness remains at the base of the tub. Bulk ferment for 4 to 5 hours at 24C, performing a set of coil folds every 45 minutes for the first three hours. The bulk is finished when the dough has risen by roughly 50%, feels aerated, and shows a domed surface with visible bubbles at the edge of the tub. Divide into two pieces, pre-shape lightly and bench rest for 25 minutes. Shape into boules, place seam side up in floured bannetons, and cold retard in the refrigerator at 4C for 12 to 16 hours. Bake straight from the refrigerator in a preheated cast iron combo cooker. Bake at 250C for 20 minutes with the lid on, then remove the lid, drop the oven to 230C and bake for a further 25 minutes until the crust is deep brown and the internal temperature reaches 96C. Cool on a rack for at least 2 hours before cutting. ## Allergen Note Contains wheat and rye, therefore contains gluten. Contains no dairy, no egg and no nuts. Suitable for vegans. Produced in a bakery that also handles milk, egg and sesame.

# Sourdough Focaccia ## Ingredients Baker's percentages are calculated against the 1000 g of strong white flour. Final hydration is 85%. | Ingredient | Weight | Baker's % | |---|---|---| | Strong white bread flour | 1000 g | 100% | | Water (24C) | 850 g | 85% | | Rye levain (100% hydration) | 250 g | 25% | | Fine sea salt | 22 g | 2.2% | | Extra virgin olive oil | 60 g | 6% | Total dough weight is 2182 g, which fills one 30 x 40 cm tray. ## Method Mix the flour and 800 g of the water until no dry flour remains and rest for 45 minutes. Reserve the last 50 g of water for the salt. Add the levain and mix through, then rest 30 minutes. Add the fine sea salt with the reserved water and squeeze until fully incorporated. Finally drizzle in the olive oil and work it in. The dough will look broken and greasy at first and will come back together after two minutes of folding. Bulk ferment for 3 to 4 hours at 24C with four sets of coil folds spaced 30 minutes apart. At 85% hydration the dough is slack, so use a wet hand and lift rather than stretch. Oil the tray generously, tip the dough in without deflating it, and spread it gently towards the corners. If it springs back, wait 20 minutes and try again rather than forcing it. Cold retard in the refrigerator for 12 hours. Bring the tray to room temperature for 90 minutes before baking. Dimple the surface firmly with oiled fingertips, pressing all the way down to the tray so the dough does not dome, then drizzle with a further tablespoon of olive oil and scatter with flaky salt. Bake at 240C for 22 minutes until the top is deep golden and the underside is crisp when lifted with a spatula. Lift the focaccia straight out of the tray onto a rack so the base does not steam. ## Allergen Note Contains wheat and rye, therefore contains gluten. Contains no dairy, no egg and no nuts. Suitable for vegans.

# Rye Levain Starter ## Ingredients This is a 100% hydration levain, meaning the water weight equals the flour weight. Baker's percentages are calculated against the 100 g of rye flour. | Ingredient | Weight | Baker's % | |---|---|---| | Wholegrain rye flour | 100 g | 100% | | Water (26C) | 100 g | 100% | | Mature sourdough starter | 20 g | 20% | Total levain yield is 220 g, which is enough to build the 400 g of levain required by the 2kg Country Sourdough after one further refreshment. ## Method Weigh the mature starter into a clear straight-sided jar and mark the level with an elastic band so the rise can be judged by eye rather than by guesswork. Add the water at 26C and stir until the starter is dispersed and the liquid turns cloudy. Add the wholegrain rye flour and mix to a thick paste. Rye holds far more water than white flour, so at 100% hydration this will look like a stiff batter rather than a dough. Cover loosely and ferment for 8 to 12 hours at 22 to 24C. The levain is ripe when it has at least doubled from the elastic band mark, the surface is domed and covered in fine bubbles, and it smells sharply sour with a faint acetone note. A levain that has risen and then collapsed back to a flat, watery surface has gone past ripe and will give a slack, over-acidified dough. The float test is a useful confirmation: drop a teaspoon of ripe levain into room temperature water and it should float rather than sink. Refresh at least once every 24 hours if the starter is kept at room temperature, or once a week if it is stored at 4C in the refrigerator. ## Allergen Note Contains rye, therefore contains gluten. Contains no dairy, no egg and no nuts. Suitable for vegans.

# Sourdough Brioche ## Ingredients Baker's percentages are calculated against the 500 g of strong white flour. This is an enriched dough, so the fat and egg percentages are high. | Ingredient | Weight | Baker's % | |---|---|---| | Strong white bread flour | 500 g | 100% | | Whole milk (cold) | 150 g | 30% | | Eggs (about 4 medium) | 200 g | 40% | | Unsalted butter (softened) | 200 g | 40% | | Caster sugar | 60 g | 12% | | Rye levain (100% hydration) | 100 g | 20% | | Fine sea salt | 10 g | 2% | Total dough weight is 1220 g, which makes two loaves in 900 g tins. ## Method Mix the flour, cold milk, eggs, sugar and levain in a stand mixer with the dough hook on low for 4 minutes until a shaggy dough forms. Add the fine sea salt and mix on medium for a further 8 minutes until the dough is smooth and pulls cleanly from the sides of the bowl. Only now begin adding the softened butter, roughly 50 g at a time, waiting until each addition has fully disappeared before adding the next. The butter goes in last and gradually, because adding it at the start coats the flour in fat and prevents the gluten network from developing at all. Expect this stage to take 10 to 12 minutes. The dough is ready when it passes the windowpane test: a small piece stretched thin should become translucent without tearing. Bulk ferment for 5 to 6 hours at 22C, then cold retard for 14 to 18 hours at 4C. Enriched sourdough is very difficult to shape at room temperature, so the cold retard is a handling step as much as a flavour step. Divide, shape into four balls per tin, and prove for 4 to 5 hours at 24C until the dough reaches the rim of the tin and springs back slowly when pressed. Egg wash and bake at 180C for 30 minutes until deep golden and the internal temperature reaches 92C. Turn out of the tins immediately to stop the sides collapsing. ## Allergen Note Contains wheat and rye, therefore contains gluten. Contains milk and butter, therefore contains dairy. Contains egg, both in the dough and in the egg wash. Contains no nuts. Suitable for vegetarians but not for vegans.

# Focaccia ## Description Focaccia is a Ligurian flatbread made from a very wet, high-hydration dough that is dimpled with the fingertips, drenched in olive oil and a salty brine, and baked until the top is golden and the interior is open and airy. The high water content is what produces the large irregular holes, and the brine poured into the dimples is what gives focaccia its characteristic soft, slightly moist crust. It requires patience rather than skill, since the dough is too wet to knead by hand and does most of its work during a long rise. It contains gluten and is naturally vegan. ## Ingredients For the dough: - Strong bread flour - 500g - Water - 400ml, lukewarm - Instant yeast - 7g - Fine salt - 10g - Honey or sugar - 1 teaspoon - Extra virgin olive oil - 60ml, plus more for the tin For the topping brine: - Water - 60ml, lukewarm - Extra virgin olive oil - 45ml - Flaky sea salt - 1.5 teaspoons - Fresh rosemary - 2 sprigs, leaves picked - Cherry tomatoes or olives - a handful (optional) ## Instructions 1. Whisk the yeast and honey into the lukewarm water and let it stand for 5 minutes until it foams. 2. Combine the flour and salt in a large bowl. Pour in the yeast water and 30ml of the olive oil, and mix with a spatula or wet hand until no dry flour remains. The dough will be very wet and sticky, which is correct. 3. Cover and rest for 15 minutes. 4. Instead of kneading, perform a set of stretch and folds: with a wet hand, reach under one side of the dough, stretch it upward and fold it over the centre. Rotate the bowl and repeat four times. 5. Repeat this folding set three more times at 30-minute intervals. The dough will transform from a shaggy mass into a smooth, elastic one. 6. Cover and leave to rise at room temperature for 2 hours, or refrigerate overnight for a much better flavour. It should double and be full of bubbles. 7. Pour 30ml of olive oil into a 30 x 20cm baking tin and spread it over the base and sides. 8. Tip the dough into the tin without deflating it too much. Fold it over itself once, then leave it to relax for 20 minutes. 9. Gently stretch the dough towards the corners of the tin. If it springs back, wait 15 minutes and try again rather than forcing it. 10. Prove uncovered in a warm place for 45 to 60 minutes until visibly puffy and jiggly. 11. Preheat the oven to 220C. Whisk the brine ingredients together. 12. Oil your fingers and press them straight down into the dough all over, right to the bottom of the tin, making deep dimples. This is what stops the focaccia from rising into a loaf. 13. Pour the brine evenly over the surface so it pools in

Lift the focaccia out of the tin immediately onto a rack so the base does not steam and go soft. Cool for at least 15 minutes before cutting. ## Tips - Resist adding flour to the sticky dough; the high hydration is what creates the open crumb. - Dimple firmly, all the way down to the tin, or the surface will dome. - The brine looks like too much liquid but is absorbed during baking and keeps the crumb moist. - An overnight cold rise gives a noticeably better flavour and a more open structure. ## Variations - Focaccia Genovese: the classic plain version with just oil, salt and brine. - Focaccia con Cipolle: topped with thinly sliced onions softened in oil. - Focaccia Barese: topped with cherry tomatoes and olives, pressed deep into the dough. - Sweet focaccia: brushed with oil and sugar and topped with grapes, a harvest speciality. ## Substitutions - Plain flour can replace bread flour, though the crumb will be less chewy. - Dried rosemary (1 teaspoon) can replace fresh. - Any good olive oil works, but this is a bread built on olive oil, so use one you like the taste of. - Gluten-free bread flour blends can be used with a 10 percent reduction in water. ## Serving Suggestions Serve focaccia warm or at room temperature, cut into squares, as part of an antipasto spread, alongside soup, or split horizontally as sandwich bread. In Liguria it is eaten for breakfast dipped in cappuccino. It is also excellent served with a bowl of good olive oil and balsamic vinegar. ## Storage Focaccia is at its best on the day it is baked. Store it wrapped in a paper bag or loosely in foil at room temperature for up to 2 days; refrigeration makes it stale quickly. Refresh it in a 180C oven for 5 minutes. It freezes well for up to 2 months, either whole or in slices; reheat directly from frozen at 180C for 10 minutes. ## Nutrition Approximate values per serving: - Calories: 330 kcal - Protein: 7 g - Carbohydrates: 48 g - Fat: 12 g - Fiber: 2 g

# Traditional Napa Cabbage Kimchi ## Ingredients Percentages here are calculated against the 2000 g of prepared napa cabbage rather than against flour, since this is a vegetable ferment rather than a dough. | Ingredient | Weight | Percentage of cabbage | |---|---|---| | Napa cabbage | 2000 g | 100% | | Coarse sea salt (for brining) | 160 g | 8% | | Gochugaru (Korean chilli flakes) | 100 g | 5% | | Korean radish, julienned | 400 g | 20% | | Garlic, minced | 60 g | 3% | | Ginger, grated | 20 g | 1% | | Saeujeot (salted fermented shrimp) | 60 g | 3% | | Anchovy fish sauce | 60 g | 3% | | Glutinous rice flour | 30 g | 1.5% | | Caster sugar | 20 g | 1% | Total yield is approximately 2.9 kg of finished kimchi. ## Method Quarter the cabbage lengthwise keeping the core attached, then brine it using the full 160 g of coarse sea salt, working the salt between the leaves and concentrating it on the thick white stems. Leave for 4 to 6 hours, turning every 2 hours. The cabbage is correctly brined when a thick white stem bends into a U shape without snapping. This bend test matters more than the clock, because cabbage size and moisture content vary considerably between heads. Rinse three times in cold water and drain cut side down for at least one hour. # Rye Levain Starter ## Ingredients This is a 100% hydration levain, meaning the water weight equals the flour weight. Baker's percentages are calculated against the 100 g of rye flour. | Ingredient | Weight | Baker's % | |---|---|---| | Wholegrain rye flour | 100 g | 100% | | Water (26C) | 100 g | 100% | | Mature sourdough starter | 20 g | 20% | Total levain yield is 220 g, which is enough to build the 400 g of levain required by the 2kg Country Sourdough after one further refreshment. ## Method Weigh the mature starter into a clear straight-sided jar and mark the level with an elastic band so the rise can be judged by eye rather than by guesswork. Rye holds far more water than white flour, so at 100% hydration this will look like a stiff batter rather than a dough. Cover loosely and ferment for 8 to 12 hours at 22 to 24C. Refresh at least once every 24 hours if the starter is kept at room temperature, or once a week if it is stored at 4C in the refrigerator. ## Allergen Note Contains rye, therefore contains gluten. Contains no dairy, no egg and no nuts. Suitable for vegans.

Recipe: Focaccia (recipe_id: recipe_066)
Section: Description

Focaccia is a Ligurian flatbread made from a very wet, high-hydration dough that is dimpled with the fingertips, drenched in olive oil and a salty brine, and baked until the top is golden and the interior is open and airy. The high water content is what produces the large irregular holes, and the brine poured into the dimples is what gives focaccia its characteristic soft, slightly moist crust. It requires patience rather than skill, since the dough is too wet to knead by hand and does most of its work during a long rise. It contains gluten and is naturally vegan.
